references.text: Jesus asked the woman to fetch her husband, and she replied that she had no husband. Jesus confirmed that she spoke the truth – which leads directly to the revelation in verse 18 about her five previous husbands ([ref:Joh 4:16-17|John 4:16-17]).
The woman herself later testified that Jesus told her everything she had done, referring back to his supernatural knowledge of her five husbands ([ref:Joh 4:29|John 4:29]).
Many Samaritans came to believe because of the woman's testimony: "He told me all that I have done", pointing back to Jesus' revelation of her marital history ([ref:Joh 4:39|John 4:39]).

Jesus' supernatural knowledge of people is also shown in his encounter with Nathanael, where Jesus knew about him before Philip called him – parallel to his knowledge of the Samaritan woman's past ([ref:Joh 1:47-48|John 1:47-48]).
John states that Jesus knew all people and what was in man, which explains his detailed knowledge of the woman's life ([ref:Joh 2:24-25|John 2:24-25]).

Historical background for the Samaritans' religious mixture: The Assyrians settled foreign peoples in Samaria, who worshipped their own gods alongside the Lord. The woman's five husbands have been seen as a possible symbolic parallel to the five nations and their gods brought to Samaria ([ref:2 Kong 17:24-33|2 Kings 17:24-33]).

The Mosaic law on divorce and remarriage provides background for understanding the woman's situation with five previous husbands. The law allowed divorce under certain conditions ([ref:5 Mos 24:1-4|Deuteronomy 24:1-4]).
Jesus' teaching on marriage and divorce sheds light on the moral dimension of the woman's situation involving repeated divorces and cohabitation without marriage ([ref:Mark 10:11-12|Mark 10:11-12]).
